body.en: Angles measured in radians give clean formulas for arc length and sector area.
\( 180^{\circ}=\pi \) radians. Arc length \( s=r\theta \); sector area \( A=\tfrac12 r^{2}\theta \), with \( \theta \) in radians.

Unit Circle Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & Triangle Laws: Every angle \(\theta\) on the unit circle defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) where \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).

body.en:
Calculator in Radian mode: Formulas \(s = r\theta\), \(A = \tfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta\), and \(A_{\Delta} = \tfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta\) are strictly valid only when \(\theta\) is in radians. If your calculator is in degree mode when evaluating \(\sin(1.2)\), you will evaluate the sine of \(1.2^\circ\) instead of \(1.2\text{ rad}\), wiping out all accuracy marks.

Perimeter of a sector: The perimeter of a sector consists of the curved arc length PLUS the two straight radii: \(P = r\theta + 2r\). Overlooking the two radii (\(+2r\)) is the single most common slip in Cambridge circular measure questions.

Major vs Minor: Always double check whether the question specifies the minor or major segment/sector. For the major sector, the central angle is \(2\pi - \theta\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Circular Measure)

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

Find the arc length when \( r=5 \) and \( \theta=\tfrac{\pi}{3} \).

\[ s=5\cdot\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{5\pi}{3}. \]

A sector OAB has radius 8 cm and angle \(\angle AOB=1.2\) rad. Find the area of the minor segment cut off by chord AB.

\[\text{Sector area}=\tfrac{1}{2}(8)^2(1.2)=38.4\text{ cm}^2.\]\[\text{Triangle area}=\tfrac{1}{2}(8)^2\sin(1.2)=32\sin(1.2)\approx29.56\text{ cm}^2.\]\[\text{Segment}=38.4-29.56\approx8.84\text{ cm}^2.\]

Problem (Easy): In the plane, the ellipse \( u: \dfrac{s^2}{2401} + \dfrac{y^2}{529} = 1 \) has foci at \( (\pm c, 0) \). Find the squared focal distance \( c^2 \) of \( u \).

Step-by-Step Solution: For an ellipse, \( c^2 = a^2 - b^2 = 2401 - 529 = 1872 \).

Problem (Medium): For real angle \( s \), suppose \( \sin(s) + \cos(s) = \dfrac{\sqrt{20}}{\sqrt{7}} \). Find the trigonometric expression \( u = 7\sin(2s) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Squaring both sides gives \( 1 + \sin(2s) = \frac{20}{7} \implies 7\sin(2s) = 13 \).

body.en: All-Solutions Checklist (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): When solving \(\trig(kx + \phi) = c\) on \([0, 2\pi]\), immediately write down the transformed interval \(\phi \le u \le 2k\pi + \phi\), list all ASTC quadrant angles in that range, and only divide by \(k\) at the very last step.

question.en: A circle has radius \(8\text{ cm}\). A sector of this circle has a total perimeter of \(28\text{ cm}\). Find the angle of the sector in radians, and calculate the exact area of the sector.

solution.en:
The perimeter of a sector is given by \(P = s + 2r = r\theta + 2r\).
Substitute \(P = 28\) and \(r = 8\): \[28 = 8\theta + 2(8) \Rightarrow 28 = 8\theta + 16 \Rightarrow 8\theta = 12 \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{12}{8} = 1.5\text{ radians}\] The area of the sector is: \[A = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}(8^2)(1.5) = \dfrac{1}{2}(64)(1.5) = 32 \times 1.5 = 48\text{ cm}^2\]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Circular Measure and start from \(8\text{ cm}\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(P = s + 2r = r\theta + 2r\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: In a circle of radius \(10\text{ cm}\), chord \(AB\) subtends an angle of \(\theta = \tfrac{2\pi}{3}\) radians at the centre \(O\). Find: (a) the exact length of chord \(AB\), (b) the exact area of the minor segment bounded by chord \(AB\) and minor arc \(AB\), in terms of \(\pi\) and \(\sqrt{3}\).

solution.en:
(a) Use the cosine rule in triangle \(OAB\) with \(OA = OB = 10\) and \(\angle AOB = \tfrac{2\pi}{3} = 120^\circ\): \[AB^2 = 10^2 + 10^2 - 2(10)(10)\cos\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 100 + 100 - 200\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = 200 + 100 = 300\] Thus \(AB = \sqrt{300} = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\).
(b) Area of sector \(OAB\): \[A_{\text{sector}} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}(10^2)\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{100\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2\] Area of triangle \(OAB\): \[A_{\Delta} = \dfrac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}(10^2)\sin\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 50\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2\] Area of minor segment: \[A_{\text{segment}} = A_{\text{sector}} - A_{\Delta} = \dfrac{100\pi}{3} - 25\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{100\pi - 75\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{ cm}^2\]

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(OAB\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.
